descriptions.text: Gnomish Knock-Knock. Type: Fuel-air bomb. Effect: Thermobaric Explosion. Status: 40. Barely stable. I wouldn't be tapping on the thing. Ever seen a hundred Dromedarians die because their lungs imploded, followed by their skin getting melted off their body just before they all shatter into mist? Well now's your chance! Fun for the whole family, this was the main weapon of the Gnomish Bombardier Squads. There are only a few of these things left, and they're usually strapped to the failing air force's most reliable patrol ships. The fuel-air Knock-Knocks were once used to devastating effect in the early days of the last conflict. The remaining munitions are instead used as a mutual-standoff weapon. …

beats.headline: Under a rowboat-sized airship
beats.text: Through a telescope, Carl looks the Wasteland over: a jagged island held aloft by colossal balloons, its edges dotted with ballistae and trebuchets. A rowboat-sized gnomish airship drifts into view on four propellers, and dangling under it is a refrigerator-sized bomb. Zoomed in, the telescope gives him the item, status 40, barely stable, with an adjustable pressure fuse that sets the height it bursts at. Carl asks Skarn whether they dropped one of those on his old village. Yep, says the kid. It was a long time ago, though, and he does not remember it.

beats.headline: Three miles of range
beats.text: To hit one of the Knock-Knocks parked under the gnomes' castle from the surface, the missiles need a range of about three miles. The missiles now burn a propellant Mordecai improved, with a second stage that lights when the first burns out, and recycling a few impact hob-lobbers showed Carl a simpler trigger, which leaves room for a full stick of hobgoblin dynamite in each warhead. The test shot chases Ruckus as the boss climbs. The second stage sparks, and the missile blows a few hundred feet short.

beats.headline: Four missiles, then three bombs
beats.text: The Wasteland has come down to about two and a half kilometres, and its underside crawls with harnessed gnomes arming bombs: dozens of small round ones, and the few Knock-Knocks left. They drop them by cutting the chains. From the hijacked balloon, at the very edge of his missiles' range, Carl fires the four guided missiles he has assigned to the Knock-Knocks he spied after sunrise, just as the airship's gun battery fires at the balloon, and all four detonate early as they cross its volley. He aims the second launcher at the battery and three bombs on the underside. The three of them leap from the basket, and the whole world to the north explodes in a ball of white, hot fire.

relations.note: the last few hang on chains under its belly
